issue_context.title: Projection pushdown with hive partitions may not be respected
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
from pathlib import Path


root = Path(".env/data2")

dfs = [
    pl.DataFrame({"x": 1}),
    pl.DataFrame({"x": 2}),
]

paths = [
    root / "a=1/b=1/data.bin",
    root / "a=2/b=2/data.bin",
]

[
    [paths[i].parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True), dfs[i].write_parquet(paths[i])]
    for i in range(len(dfs))
]

lf = pl.scan_parquet(root / "**/*.bin")
lf = lf.select("x", "a")

print(lf.collect())
```
Observe the `select` was not respected:
```python
shape: (2, 3)
┌─────┬─────┬─────┐
│ x   ┆ a   ┆ b   │
│ --- ┆ --- ┆ --- │
│ i64 ┆ i64 ┆ i64 │
╞═════╪═════╪═════╡
│ 1   ┆ 1   ┆ 1   │
│ 2   ┆ 2   ┆ 2   │
└─────┴─────┴─────┘
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/15573 removes the projection node after projection pushdown into the parquet reader, which reveals that the parquet reader was not applying the projection properly on the hive partition columns.

### Expected behavior

```python
shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬─────┐
│ x   ┆ a   │
│ --- ┆ --- │
│ i64 ┆ i64 │
╞═════╪═════╡
│ 1   ┆ 1   │
│ 2   ┆ 2   │
└─────┴─────┘
```

review_comments: This is the fix for the corrupted reads in `read_async` - the index here is relative to the current batch.

I discovered there was other code in place to ensure the invariant that a reader always has at least one path here, it would replace the scan node with a `DataFrameScan` but it wasn't being hit because it was incorrectly checking the old `paths` instead of `new_paths`. This changes the fix at https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/12575
